sentences.text: ( LAND ACQUISITION) APPEAL SUIT NO: 2997/2004

Between:
The Land Acquisition Officer (sw) ...APPELLANT  AND Saripalli Laxmi Died and Others ...RESPONDENT(S)
Counsel for the Appellant: 1.

GP FOR APPEALS Counsel for the Respondent(S): 1.
The Court made the following JUDGMENT: (per NJS,J) Heard Mr. T S Rayulu, learned counsel for the appellant.
Despite service of notice, none entered appearance on behalf of the respondents.

2. Aggrieved by the order of the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Visakhapatnam dated 18.04.2003 in O.P. No.222 of 1990 enhancing the compensation from Rs.30,000/- to Rs.60,000/- per acre, the State filed the present appeal.

3. For the purpose of providing house sites to weaker section families, an extent of Ac.0.48 cents in Survey No.44/2 of Madhurawada Village was acquired and an Award No.2/84 dated 16.03.1984 was passed.

The claimants/respondents, aggrieved by the fixation of the market value at Rs.30,000/-
per acre, sought reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, seeking enhancement of compensation before the Reference Court.
Contd...
NJS,J & TMR,J 4.

On behalf of the respondents/ claimants, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Exs.A1 and A2 i.e.,
Certified copy of the Common Judgment in O.P No.78 of 1988 and etc., dated 01.11.1994, and Certified copy of the sale deed were marked.

No oral and documentary evidence was adduced on The Land Acquisition Officer Sw vs Saripalli Laxmi Died on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177585666/
1 behalf of the Referring Officer.

sentences.text:
The learned Reference Court, taking into consideration Ex.A1,
enhanced the compensation from Rs.30,000/- to Rs.60,000/- per acre.
Assailing the said enhancement, the present appeal is filed.

5. The learned Government Pleader submits that the enhancement of the compensation is without any valid basis and no cogent evidence is placed before the learned Reference Court by the claimants for the enhancement sought for.

He submits that the learned Reference Court further went wrong in not deducting the development charges, while enhancing the compensation and as such, the order under challenge warrants interference by this Court.
6. We have considered the submissions made and perused the material on record.

On an appreciation of the submissions made, the only point that falls for consideration is:
"Whether the fixation of compensation @ Rs.60,000/- per acre by the learned Reference Court, is excessive and warrants interference by this Court, in the facts and circumstances of the case?"
7.

In support of the claim for enhancement, the respondents/claimants relied on Ex.A1 i.e.,
Judgment in O.P No.78 of 1988, apart from oral adducing evidence.

Prior to acquisition of the subject matter lands, which are situate in Survey No.44/2 of Madhurawada Village, it would appear that the lands in Survey Nos.34, 37 and 39 of the same village were acquired and Award No.1/85 was passed, in respect of the said lands.
It would appear that Section 4(1) Notification in respect of the lands covered under Ex.A1 was issued in the same month, as in the case of lands in the present case.

In respect of the lands acquired under Ex.A1-Award No.1/85, on reference, the compensation was enhanced from Rs.30,000/- to Rs.60,000/- per acre vide Order dated Contd...
NJS,J & TMR,J 01.11.1994 in O.P No.78 of 1988, 10/1989 and batch.
No material is placed to show that the said enhancement is not approved by the appellate Court.
8. Be that as it may.

The learned Reference Court, while taking into consideration the said orders passed in respect of the lands situate in the very same village i.e., Madhurawada and by taking into consideration the potentiality and proximity held that the respondents/claimants are entitled for compensation @ Rs.60,000/- per acre, as against Rs.30,000/- fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer.
Therefore, we see no reason to arrive at a conclusion that the fixation is without any valid basis as argued by the learned Government Pleader for Appeals.
9. With regard to the other contention that the learned Reference Court had committed error in not making deductions of development charges, the same deserves no appreciation.

In fact, the learned Reference Court, while taking into consideration Ex.A1, had categorically held that the lands acquired are already developed and nothing more is required to be done to convert them into house sites by leveling etc.
10.
In the light of the well considered order of the learned Reference Court supported by cogent reasons, this Court is of the firm view that the order under challenge warrants no interference.

2 is answered accordingly.
